Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can produce an operational erasure playbook and a deletion certificate; a few details below and I attached our current draft playbook for your procurement/legal review.

High-level points (details and evidence in the attached):
- EU-only enforcement: data plane routes and storage are pinned to EU regions; control plane metadata (non-PII telemetry) is logically separated and can be restricted to a customer-controlled VPC; SCCs are applied for cross-border fallbacks with supplemental technical measures documented.
- Deletion timelines: typical hot-store TTLs can be sub-24 hours for session artifacts; object store (standard) snapshots: standard retention 30 days by default, but we offer contractable expedited purge options with a guaranteed proof-of-deletion within 7 days and a signed deletion certificate.
- Backups: periodic snapshots (region-local) retained 30 days; isolated snapshot purge is possible; for customers needing shorter windows we support a 7-day SLA for full wipe and supporting artifact evidence.
- Operator access: role-based with just-in-time bastion jump, session recording and 2-person approval for any operator-initiated deletion. We can provide audit logs showing operator identity + session transcripts.
- KMS: EU CMKs supported via customer-managed keys in our EU KMS region (integrates with customer KMS/HSM).

Next steps: 1) attached draft playbook (RWI_ERASURE_PLAYBOOK_v0.9.pdf) — Naomi and Karthik, please review and add the certificate template + exact tech commands for removal from snapshots; 2) Anna, if convenient, let's book a 30-min runbook walkthrough early next week to run through the evidence artifacts and any redlines.

Thanks,

Naomi / team — technical confirmations to include in the playbook: 

- Snapshot / backup retention: default 30-day rolling snapshots in EU region. For expedited purge: we commit to a 7-calendar-day full purge SLA for contractually-bound customers; the purge process removes object pointers, then issues a garbage collection pass to zero out blocks (where underlying storage supports it) and remove index entries.
- Signed manifest: yes — we can produce a manifest (JSON lines of object keys + sizes + checksum) and sign it with our operational signing key; the manifest will reference snapshot id and S3 object path (region-located) and will be accompanied by the audit log entry id.
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported via EU KMS (we can accept a CMK ARN or integrate with HSM vaults). We will record the CMK id in the deletion certificate.
- Operator access: all access requires ephemeral bastion session with recorded tty and duration; operators must have 2-person approval for purge actions. Session recordings are stored in-region and can be redacted for PII before sharing.
- Logs / proof: audit logs kept 90 days; we can export signed log snapshots as part of the evidence bundle.

I'll add a short technical appendix to the draft with command examples and the exact manifest schema.

-Karthik
